comparison: Strong agreement on the two-step model for PCP formation (C37-C47). Both evaluations find the mosaic experiments and transplantation data compelling and accept that this model excludes the long-range Wnt3-gradient alternative. OpenEval notes the small sample size for rosette formation but finds evidence sufficient; peer reviewers accepted findings without this caveat.

Strong agreement on the genetic separation of Wnt3's dual roles (C30-C35). Both evaluations find the dnTCF and CA-β-catenin experiments convincing in demonstrating independence of PCP-orienting function from β-catenin signaling. Peer reviewers called this 'the surprising result of this study' and accepted it without criticism.

Strong agreement on Wnt3's dual role and non-autonomous PCP rescue (C4-C6, C18-C20). Both evaluations find the rescue experiments compelling. OpenEval also includes C36, C59-C61 in this grouping, while peer review focuses on the core PCP phenotype claims (C15, C17). All reviewers praised these findings as elegant and sophisticated.

Agreement on mechanical cues triggering PCP reorientation (C48-C52, C54). Both evaluations accept the transplantation experiments showing alternative PCP orientation mechanisms. OpenEval notes small sample size (N=3/8 for rosettes) but finds data consistent with mechanical strain effects; peer reviewers accepted observations as supporting model flexibility.

Agreement on temporal dynamics of PCP establishment (C21-C23, C25-C27). Both evaluations accept the time-course and live imaging data. Peer reviewer noted the mechanism of signal propagation remains unclear but did not challenge the observational data itself. OpenEval includes additional claims (C12-C14, C28-C29) about gradual coordination vs. wave-like propagation.

Disagreement on evolutionary framework (C91-C94, C98-C100). OpenEval finds genomic analysis and phylogenetic claims appropriately cautious and supported. Peer reviewer raised concerns about bias toward traditional choanzoan-sponge ancestry, recommending incorporation of Ctenophora-sister hypothesis. Both agree claims require careful interpretation but differ on adequacy of current framing.

Partial disagreement on comparative evolutionary conclusions (C74-C76, C78). OpenEval finds claims appropriately supported by citations, though notes some speculation. Peer reviewer raised specific concern about Wnt7 expression potentially challenging the evolutionary implications about Wnt subtype usage, suggesting these conclusions require further investigation.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding molecular mechanisms (C67-C68). Both evaluations note that CheFz1's role is speculative without direct experimental evidence. OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN; peer reviewer notes the molecular basis for Wnt3-PCP interaction remains unresolved. Both agree mechanism requires further investigation.

Agreement on PCP defects from Wnt3 depletion (C15-C17). OpenEval finds quantitative PCP analysis data convincing. Peer review includes these claims with the broader dual role findings (C5-C6, C18-C20) and accepts them as part of the compelling evidence package without specific criticism.

Agreement on RhoABC's role in PCP-mediated morphogenesis (C55). Both evaluations accept morphological observations of RhoABC-DN embryos. OpenEval treats this as a separate finding; peer reviewer groups it with mechanical cue observations (C56-C58) as supporting mechanotransduction.

Agreement on Fat/Ds involvement in Clytia PCP (C82). Both evaluations accept the supplementary data without specific criticism. OpenEval provides more detailed assessment noting overlapping roles with Wnt3; peer reviewer implicitly accepted by not raising concerns.

Agreement on evolutionary implications of dual Wnt3 role (C59-C61, C63). OpenEval includes these in central findings group; peer reviewers accepted the evolutionary significance for understanding axis formation and pathway origins. Both note the dual role as a major finding with evolutionary implications.

Agreement on morphogenetic requirements (C87). Both evaluations accept claims about elongation requiring both PCP and gastrulation. OpenEval includes broader comparative claims (C85-C86, C88); peer reviewer implicitly accepted by not challenging the partial rescue data.

Partial overlap on mechanism uncertainty (C66). OpenEval includes C66 in two-step model support group; peer reviewer notes the molecular basis for local Wnt3 action remains unresolved. Both acknowledge mechanism requires further study but OpenEval finds current evidence sufficient for the two-step model.

OpenEval evaluated the conceptual framework and prior knowledge context (C1-C3, C7-C11) as well-supported by established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these background claims were not specifically discussed by reviewers.

Minor overlap on elongation requirements (C33). OpenEval includes this in genetic separation findings; peer reviewer accepts it as part of morphogenetic requirements. Both agree on the data showing elongation requires both PCP and gastrulation mechanisms.

Overlap on evolutionary significance (C63, C73). OpenEval groups these with broader comparative conclusions; peer reviewers accepted the evolutionary implications for understanding pathway origins. Both find the dual role has significant evolutionary implications though peer reviewer raised concerns about Wnt subtype interpretation.

Overlap on RhoABC manipulation supporting mechanical reorientation (C56-C58). OpenEval treats RhoABC data as independent support for mechanical PCP reorientation; peer reviewer groups with mechanotransduction observations. Both accept the data as supporting evidence.

Minor overlap on dual role implications (C36). OpenEval includes this in central findings about Wnt3's dual role; peer reviewer focuses on the independence of the two functions. Both accept the finding but group related claims differently.

Minor overlap on two-step model implications (C64). OpenEval includes this in two-step model support; peer reviewer discusses it in context of evolutionary significance. Both accept the finding but emphasize different aspects.
